sections.h2: Where to file a deed in Jackson County
sections.html:
Go upstairs to the third floor. The Recorder sits inside the courthouse at 226 East Main Street, Jackson, OH 45640, phone (740) 286-1919, fax (740) 286-8835. The office runs 8:30 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays and shuts for lunch between 11:30 am and 12:30 pm, so plan to arrive outside that gap.

Payment may be cash, a check or a debit or credit card, and the card route adds a $2.00 service fee. The county's official records begin in 1997. Anything older must be viewed and printed at the office, while later records are searchable online after you set up an account.

Most recordable papers, from deeds and mortgages to leases and affidavits, cost $39.00 for two pages and $8.00 for every further page, counting each printed side separately. Ohio sets these amounts, with one half paying for the basic recording fee and the other half going to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund.

Jackson County Recorder fees
Document or serviceFee
Recording a deed, mortgage or lease (two pages included)$39.00
Each page past two$8.00
Marginal notation on a release, assignment or amendment$4.00 each
Plat or condominium drawing, each 8 by 14 sheet$40.00
Real estate UCC financing statement$12.00 plus $4.00 per name indexed
Plain copy$2.00 a page
Certified copy$2.00 a page, plus $1.00 for the seal

A veteran's service discharge and one certified copy carry no fee, and a zoning resolution costs $50.00.

sections.h2: What the Auditor adds before recording
sections.html:
Two charges are printed on the Auditor's real estate transfers page: a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand and a transfer fee of fifty cents per parcel. The conveyance fee jumped from $1.00 per thousand of the purchase price on March 24, 1993.

The Auditor works in the same building, 226 East Main Street, Suite 5, phone (740) 286-4231, opening at 8:00 am and closing at 4:00 pm. Under the Auditor's Tools menu you will find a Conveyance Calculator and a Sales Reports page. The seller carries the cost, since R.C. 319.202(D) charges the grantor. Forms on the site include:

  • DTE 100, the value statement that doubles as the fee receipt
  • DTE 100EX, the reason an exemption applies
  • DTE 100M and 100MEX, the manufactured and mobile home versions

The order is Auditor, then Recorder. If you need to add or remove someone's name from title, that takes a new deed, which clears the Auditor and is then recorded.

sections.h2: What happens if a deed is never recorded
sections.html:
A second buyer can end up owning the house. R.C. 5301.25 requires a deed to be recorded in the county of the land, and until that happens it is treated as fraudulent against a later purchaser who bought in good faith.

A few things sellers often ask the Recorder:

  • Most records are public. Military service records go only to the veteran, with proof of ID.
  • A will is recorded through Probate Court, which charges $46.00.
  • Deeds and similar papers are best drafted by an attorney or other professional.

A name error means a fresh deed, which repeats the Auditor and Recorder steps.

Viewing most records online starts with an account. A deed from the 1980s predates the 1997 start of the official records and has to be pulled at the courthouse itself.

To order an image, email the document's book and page to recordersoffice@jacksoncounty.us. The charge is $2.00 a page, paid in cash or by check. Someone planning to list a house can also open the Sales Reports page on the Auditor's site, which sits alongside the Conveyance Calculator and a Tax Estimator.

The fee list covers more than deeds. These items surface when a title search finds old liens or a former owner left paperwork behind:

  • federal tax liens and other federal liens: $5.00
  • releases or partial releases of those liens: $3.00
  • a living will or durable power of attorney for health care: $40.00
  • zoning amendments: $20.00
  • no fee for personal property tax, workers' compensation, recognizance and unemployment compensation liens, or for certificates of premium due

These charges rest on R.C. 317.32 and 317.36. If an old lien shows up on your parcel, ask the Recorder which release clears it and what that costs, because a release is recorded on its own, apart from the deed.

A complaint goes to the county Board of Revision, made up of the Auditor, the Treasurer and the President of the County Commissioners, or their designees. It changes values rather than tax dollars. File form DTE 1 with the Auditor, who acts as the board's secretary. The filing deadline is March 31.

Some cautions apply. The form must show the owner's opinion of value on line 8 and be notarized. Ohio allows one filing per three-year period in general, and a withdrawn complaint still counts. Proof falls on the owner, and the outcome can be a higher value, a lower one or no change. The board will not weigh a percentage jump in the tax bill or a neighbor's lower valuation.

For payment questions, call the County Treasurer at 740-286-2402. Real estate taxes can be paid online or by the Autoagent phone line, 1-844-674-1100.

Jackson County had 32,817 residents in July 2025 and 14,665 housing units, 73.9% of them owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home is worth $150,700 and median household income is $57,106. The Auditor's site counts 28,916 parcels for 2024.

Have the deed drafted, preferably by an attorney. Sign it, then take it to Suite 5 for the Auditor's conveyance fee and transfer fee, using form DTE 100 or the exemption version. Carry the stamped deed to the third floor and pay the recording fee, remembering the lunch closure. Ask for a copy for your closing file.

faqs.q: How much does the Jackson County Recorder charge for a three-page deed?
faqs.a: $47.00, which is $39.00 for the first two pages plus $8.00 for the third. Each marginal notation adds $4.00, so ask the office whether any apply to your paper.

faqs.q: Is the Jackson County Recorder open over lunch?
faqs.a: No. The office shuts from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm, and its weekday service window is 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

faqs.q: What conveyance fee does Jackson County charge?
faqs.a: $4.00 per thousand dollars of purchase price, plus a $0.50 transfer fee for each parcel. The $4.00 rate dates to March 24, 1993.

faqs.q: Does paying the Jackson County Recorder by card cost extra?
faqs.a: Yes, by $2.00. Debit and credit cards carry that service fee, while cash and checks carry no add-on.

faqs.q: Does the Jackson County Recorder record wills?
faqs.a: No. A will is recorded in Probate Court, at a cost of $46.00. The Recorder files deeds, mortgages and similar land records.
